function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We have a tool to execute system commands. We can run a command to check if Chrome is installed. On Windows, Chrome is usually installed at "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" or "C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe". We can check existence of the file. We can use os.path.exists. But we only have cmd_controller_execute. We can run a command like "if exist \"C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe\" (echo yes) else (echo no)". Or we can use "where chrome" to see if it's in PATH. Let's use "where chrome" which returns path if found. So we can run "where chrome" and parse output. If output contains path, then installed. We'll call the function.

We need to produce a JSON with command and unit. The unit is optional. We'll set unit to "N/A". We'll call the function.
